label: paragraph_title
text: SWATOW BOYCOTT.

label: text
text: BRITAIN AND JAPAN NOT EXEMPT.

label: text
text: ANTI-RED MEASURES.

label: text
text: DECLINE OF FEELING AGAINST FOREIGNERS.

label: text
text: According to latest advices from Swatow the anti-Reids are taking measures to ensure non-interference with foreigners there and to encourage a certain amount of trade but the Seamen's and Firemen's Unions are still a power in the land and it is still impossible to land British or Japanese cargo in Swatow. This, a skipper who returned from Swatow yesterday was able to confirm

label: text
text: Our informant stated that there is no lack of evidence in Swatow of opposition to the Canton faction. Ships which put in with rice for Canton are allowed to discharge at Swatow but no clearance is granted. Threats were even held out to a Soviet ship from Canton on its way to Shanghai with cargo and vegetables that soldiers would be placed aboard her and the ship seized. Clearance was refused.

label: text
text: The boycott on British and Japanese goods is still enforced, said our informant, and the proclamation which has been made calling upon the people to encourage trade does not apparently apply to these. Another proclamation states that foreigners must not be interfered with and the anti-foreign feeling would certainly appear to be on the decrease. Chinese servants have not, however, returned in large numbers and the consul, for instance, is still servantless.

label: text
text: The landing of passengers which was such a difficult task during the Red régime is now comparatively simple and sampans are allowed to go alongside ships and tout for passengers. Some ricshas will carry a foreigner in the street; others will not, but it is only in the course of the last few days that even a few ricshas have been available for foreigners.

label: text
text: Our informant, brought up in a nautical school in which discipline is considered the first essential for efficiency, was most unfavourably impressed by the untidiness and lack of system on board the Soviet ships he had the opportunity of observing whilst he was in port.

label: text
text: An incident, our informant actually witnessed during a brief period ashore, was the procession of armed soldiers with Chinese in the middle with his hands tied and a large mob following. Rifle shots were heard shortly afterwards and the information was the executed man was one of the principal officials in the late Red régime at Swatow. The charge on which he was convicted was that of “squeezing” money for the Chinese and using it for his own purposes. Although the subject is hardly one to trifle with, it was stated naively to our informant that the late leader's heavy expenditure was due to the fact that he had eight wives!

label: text
text: "RED" OFFICIAL SHOT.

label: text
text: The procession which, as already reported, was nipped in the bud, was to have been for the purpose of protesting against the proclamation in favour of resumption of trade and allowing passengers ashore. The leaders were informed that the procession would be fired upon if it took place.

label: text
text:
The general opinion in Swatow appears to be that the "Reds" have to many domestic problems on hand at present to concentrate at present on the recapture of Swatow.
LOCAL INCIDENTS.
An enlargement, which can be only described as a fake, of a photo of the Shameen shooting, was found on a passenger arriving this morning on the O.S.K. steamer "Kaijo Maru" from Swatow and ports.
The owner of the picture was a Chinese. The print depicted for sign troops, under cover, and lined up for action, firing as a crowd of Chinese women with many dead bodies lying on Shakea but no Chinese soldier in. The vengeance! The owner was dealt with by the Police searchers.
Continued of foot of West Colum.

label: paragraph_title
text: PEACE NEWS.

label: text
text: TELEGRAM EXPECTED SHORTLY.

label: text
text: LAST NIGHT'S MEETING.

label: text
text: A telegram has been eagerly awaited from Canton by the sponsors of the peace delegation which went up on Monday morning. Last night the Hongkong delegates met the Canton strike authorities with a view to bringing about a settlement and it was rumoured in town that a report by telegram had been sent down.

label: text
text:
On inquiry from Mr. Wong Tong this afternoon, a “China Mail” reporter was informed that no message had arrived. However, Mr. Wong had cabled up for news as to the outcome of the conference.
Mr. Wong is the chief manager of the On Lok Yuen Co. (Hongkong and Canton) and came down from Canton when local Chinese merchants first mooted the idea of a peace talk. He has been mainly instrumental in paving the way to a conference.

label: paragraph_title
text: ABSENT PICKETS.

label: paragraph_title
text: CHINSHAN STRIKERS NOT ON DUTY

label: text
text: NEWS FROM MACAO.

label: text
text: Alleged to have been “seen off” by a detachment of Whampoa Cadets, the strike pickets are not now on duty at Chinshan, the Chinese point just outside “the Macao border and” on the main road from the Portuguese Colony into the interior.

label: text
text: Accordingly, people in the vicinity who wish to get away are taking advantage of the opportunity.

label: text
text: From small, up-country ports in the Sze Yap, batches of people are also reaching Macao, having chartered junks for the purpose. The fare is $5 a head, this high price being necessary as the junky have to pay heavily for "safe duct" through a pirate-infested area which is not on the usual route. Pickets are stationed along the usual routes, hence the necessity to trust pirates.

label: text
text: The small steamers from Kwong Hoi city to Macao are still reported to be sailing.

label: paragraph_title
text: LOCAL FOOTBALL

label: paragraph_title
text: POLICE TO PLAY AT KOWLOON.

label: text
text: SATURDAY'S MATCH

label: text
text: Proceeds from a football match will be devoted to a deserving object and the game will be played at the Kowloon Football Club's ground on Saturday, kick-off at 4.30 p.m.

label: text
text: The opposing sides will be the home team and the Police eleven. Payment is to be made at the gate.

label: text
text: The Harbour Office notifies mariners that the Engineer Co., Hongkong Volunteer Defence Corps will hold searchlight runs at Belchers Fort on-Thursday, October 1, commencing 5.30 p.m.

label: text
text: Japanese and Chinese were the majority of the hundred or so passengers who went up to Canton this morning by the Steamboat Co.'s s.s. "Honam." The departure was without incident. A proposal is being considered to run the China Navigation Co.'s s.s. "Fatshan" next week in conjunction with the Steamboat Co. as hitherto.

label: text
text: Over 200 passengers came in from Swatow on the Kalo Mart.

label: text
text:
After many conflicting reports the "Hydranges" at last sailed for Swatow, leaving yesterday afternoon. This is presumed by Chinese business men to mean a return to normal conditions at that port.
The "Hydranges" took up a full ship of cargo but few passengers. About 20 Chinese, alleged to be Whampoa Cedate who fled from Swatow when the coup was carried out against them arrived by the Douglas Co's as "Haining" and were sent back by the Hydranges.
It is expected that there will be regular communication to the two Hongkong and Swan.

label: paragraph_title
text: BORDER LOOT

label: text
text:
POLICE INTERCEPT
RAIDERS.

label: text
text: CHINENE OPEN FIRE.

label: text
text: Details of another border outrage were received from the New Territories this morning, the scene being in the Shattankok district, where the strikers made a raid last Wednesday and carried off a number of pigs valued at $2,000 and also kidnapped two grocery-skip employees.

label: text
text: Emboldened by their success on this occasion, a large body of strikers and coolies paid a visit to the same shop, the Yuan Tai Tsan, on Sunday, and removed practically everything in the shop, including some more pigs.

label: text
text: They were proceeding with their loot across the frontier near Shataukok when they were intercepted by a party of Police, who fired a shot at one of the strikers. The whole crowd then turned back, and shortly after the Police party, which included some Punjabi soldiers, were greeted with a fusilade of rifle fire from Chinese soldiers who had concealed themselves in some bushes in British territory.

label: text
text: It is estimated that about fifty shots were fired at the Police, who were fortunately not hit, and they were forced to take cover without returning the fire as the ambushed party of Chinese could not be located.

label: text
text: Advantage was taken by the men carrying the loot to get away while the Police were covered by the rifle fire of their confederates.

label: paragraph_title
text: THE BLIND HOME.

label: text
text: HOW LOCAL TALENT IS CULTIVATED.

label: text
text: MONDAY'S WORK SALE.

label: text
text:
Although the worthy nature of the work being carried on by the Blind Home is generally realised, the sale of work to be held in connection with it on Monday should serve as a reminder that substantial funds are required for its direction and it is on the sale of articles which are made there that the Home is dependent to a considerable extent for the raising of such funds.
The activities of the blind inmates are not confined to physical work and a charming illustration of how opportunity is given for the development of native gifts and talent is promised in the announced appearance of blind girl singers and violinists.

label: text
text: PRAYA JUNK'S HAUL.

label: text
text: Revenue officers of the Imports and Exports Department seized about 12,000 rounds of ammunition this morning.

label: text
text:
An ordinary cargo junk was lying alongside the western Praya, near the Sai Kong wharf (which is a little further down than the Steamboat Co.'s Wing Lok wharf) and the ammunition was found in a search on board.
The contraband is said to be of American manufacture but no information could be obtained on inquiry.

label: text

label: paragraph_title
text: “MORE SERIOUS.”

label: paragraph_title
text: CANTON REPORT ON THE STRIKE.

label: text
text: NOT "ANTI-FOREIGN."

label: text
text: Highly lauded by the "Canton Gazette" is a long survey on the recent situation in Canton by the correspondent of "an important news agency in North China."

label: text
text: The strike, strange to say, is becoming more serious owing to the strengthening of the strike organisation. It is hoped, however, that with the departure of the delegation, new developments in the strike situation may be expected. Very much depends on the nature attitude of Hongkong. Unfortunately she still demands intervention in Canton instead of pursuing a policy of reconciliation and mutual understanding. There is not the slightest trace of anti-foreignism in Canton. I learn from reliable sources that the Whampoa incident in which a Japanese launch was shot at with casualties already reported, has been settled in an amicable manner by both parties. Evidently neither side cared to give prominence to the incident. The blockade seems to have affected Canton very little. The import-export business is deeply affected, while the silk of this season has found a way out directly to Shanghai, it cannot be said that the problem of the export of silk from Kwangtung has been completely solved.

label: paragraph_title
text: BRITISH CARGO.

label: text
text: UNAFFECTED BY WHAMPOA SERVICE.

label: text
text: HUROPE TARIFF RATES.

label: text
text:
Enquiries made regarding the movement of cargo between Whampoa and Shanghai, to which reference has already been made, go to show that there has been no relaxing of the boycott against the import or export of British goods even where direct loading or unloading is done at Whampoa. So long as the present state of affairs continues at Canton the institution of indirect communication between Whampoa and Hongkong by way of Shanghai can therefore help but little, if at all, in the clearance of British cargo at present in godown in Hongkong.
In so far as direct trade between Whampoa and Europe is concerned the purely British boycott is as rigid in its application, and two German boats are thought to have been the only ones to have loaded there for Europe since the present trouble. As, however, there was no direct loading by ocean steamers at Whampoa prior to the strike and boycott, some tariff rate was considered necessary by the shipping companies concerned in the event of there being any considerable movement of cargo between Europe and Whampoa direct.

label: text
text: would naturally be somewhat higher than those in operation in Hong Kong because of the risks entailed and costs of lightenage and under

label: text
text:
a notification of this month issued by the China Homeward Conference, shippers from Europe has informed of increased freight charges by shipping companies concerned. These amount to five shillings per ton over and above Hongkong rates. shippers also to pay lightage and long time.

label: paragraph_title
text: SNUB TO REDS

label: text
text: LABOUR CONFERENCE DEFEAT.

label: text
text: COMMUNISTS NOT WANTED.

label: text
text: London, Sept. 29.

label: text
text: The Labour Conference adopted the Executive's recommendations against affiliation with the Communists by 2,600,000 against 480,000 votes rejecting the third Communist attempt to refer the matter back.

label: text
text: Complaints of the Communists that the Standing Orders were invoked to burke discussion, evoked an emphatic denial from Mr. Arthur Henderson, the Secretary who said the Executive considered it was not desirable to waste further time on a question which the Labour movement had already decided.

label: text
text: Mr. Harry Pollitt, Communist, declared that whatever the Conference did it could not keep the Communists out, adding that the Labour Party should be wide enough to include not merely those who dined at Balmoral, like Mr. Ramsay MacDonald or stayed on a yacht at Cowes with Lord Inchcape, like Mr. J. H. Thomas.

label: text
text: Mr. T. Bromley, of the locomotive Union, said the decision of the conference meant the beginning of a heresy hunt in the ranks of Trade Unions.

label: text
text: Mr. Ramsay MacDonald was ringingly cheered when he told the Communists to come out of the Trade Unions and propagate their opinions honestly outside.

label: paragraph_title
text: SEIZED SHIP.

label: text
text: PORTUGUESE BOAT AT CANTON.

label: text
text: NOW IN STRIKERS' HANDS.

label: text
text: In the early days of the strike the s.s. "Foo Chebng" was "abandoned" at Pakkai, the port of Kongmoon, through the native crew deserting.

label: text
text: Subsequently a report went round that the ship had been seized by the strikers. A Portuguese naval vessel from Macao was stated to have failed to bring the boat back and the "Foo Cheong" was last heard of in Kongmoon.

label: text
text: Saturday's "Canton Gazette" says:—Owing to the transportation of "undesirable" goods the s.s. "Foo Cheong" was detained recently by the pickets at Canton and for various reasons, the case has not been settled.

label: text
text:
The same report says that the Ning Hoi Co. wishes to charter the steamer from the strikers, for the Canton-Wuchow run, promising $1,200 a month as charter hire, and stipulating the services of 20 pickets on board "for protection."
The “Foo Cheong” was well-known on the Canton-Macao run prior to being superseded by the s.s. “Hang Cheong!” It is under Portuguese registry and when the strike started, was put on the Kongmoon-Macao run till it was forced to tie up through the crew going ashore on being intimidated at Pakkai.

label: text
text: "Wah Shan" Sequel.

label: text
text:
Negotiations are continuing for the release of the Chinese s.s. "Wah Shan" which was seized by Canton while conveying livestock from Kwong Chow Wan to Hongkong.
According to one report the owners may be willing to pay a few thousand dollars as a "fine" and it is likely that an amount may be named by the strikers holding the ship.
